title: Pool Service Invoicing Software: AutoPay, Billing & Cost
description: Pool service invoicing software compared: per-stop vs monthly rates, auto billing, AutoPay, card fees and QuickBooks for 6 pool tools, with costs.
h1: Pool service invoicing software: billing, AutoPay and QuickBooks compared
body:
Pool service billing is not like most trades. You bill the same customers every month, some per stop and some at a flat monthly rate, chemicals are either included or charged on top, and the whole route goes out in one billing run. Good pool service invoicing software builds those invoices from the stops your techs logged, emails them with a pay link, and collects by card or bank on AutoPay so you're not chasing checks. Below is what six pool-focused tools publish about billing: rate types, automatic invoicing, AutoPay, payment methods, card-fee pass-through and QuickBooks, plus what each costs. Everything comes from the vendors' own pricing, feature and help pages, checked 2026-11-24. Anything a vendor doesn't publish is marked unknown. For the overall picture, see best pool service software and the pool service hub. Routing and chemical logs are covered in pool route software and pool maintenance software.

What billing costs at two route sizes

Each tool charges on a different unit (per pool, per tech, per user or per route), so here are list prices for two example businesses, worked out from the published formulas. These are subscription prices only. Card processing, texting and other add-ons are extra, and the plan shown is the one that includes the billing features in the table above.

Pool Office Manager also lets you deactivate users in the off-season, and Skimmer doesn't bill for locations you didn't service that month. 1. Skimmer: the most published detail on pool rate types

Skimmer's help center lists four routine-service rate types: per stop with chemicals, per stop plus chemicals, per month with chemicals and per month plus chemicals. With "plus chemicals", logged dosages are added to the invoice. Auto Invoicing runs on a day of the month you pick and either sends invoices or saves them as drafts. Per-month customers can be billed ahead for the current month, while per-stop service and dosages are billed for the prior month. Work orders and stops with installed items aren't billed automatically and stay for review. Customers can enroll in AutoPay from an invoice or the customer portal and pay by card, US bank account, Apple Pay or Google Pay. Skimmer lists invoicing, online payments and surcharging on the entry Getting Started plan, and the billing page says card payouts arrive the next business day. Skimmer doesn't publish its card processing rate (billing FAQ, billing page). Full plan details: Skimmer pricing explained. {{aff:skimmer|See Skimmer plans}}

2. Pool Brain: set-and-forget monthly billing

Pool Brain's features page describes billing per visit or at a flat rate, in advance or in arrears, and automatic or manual. With automatic billing, invoices are created, charged to the card or bank account on file and emailed every month, and a declined card is retried once a day. QuickBooks Online is optional, with a two-way sync of customers, invoices, payments, refunds and products (Pool Brain features). Price: $50/mo base with unlimited office users, plus $65/mo per active field tech. Pool Brain doesn't publish a card processing rate. {{aff:poolbrain|Visit Pool Brain}}

3. Pool Office Manager: invoices built from the visit, Stripe for payments

POM builds invoices from completed service visits (labor, service call and chemicals used) and supports batch invoicing and status tracking from Draft to Paid. Payments run through Stripe (card and ACH) at Stripe's standard rates, with QuickBooks Online Payments or Biller Genie with Fortis as alternatives. QuickBooks Online two-way sync is a $25/mo add-on, and the page says POM also works with QuickBooks Desktop. AutoPay and flat monthly rates aren't described on the pricing page, so ask in the 30-day trial (POM pricing). {{aff:poolofficemanager|Visit Pool Office Manager}}

4. UpBuoy: free to try, billing extras on Professional

UpBuoy lists automatic invoice generation from service data, online payments by card and ACH, AutoPay and two-way QuickBooks Online sync (UpBuoy features). Its pricing table puts "Advanced Billing" on Professional ($3 per serviced location, $99/mo minimum) rather than the free Essential plan (up to 3 locations). UpBuoy doesn't publish which billing features are in Essential or its card rates (UpBuoy pricing). {{aff:upbuoy|Visit UpBuoy}}

5. Paythepoolman: cheapest per tech, with a customer-paid card fee option

Paythepoolman is built around billing: one-pass billing cycles with late fees and statements, invoices texted with a pay link, free overdue reminders and QuickBooks sync. Card payments and autopay are on every plan. ACH, Apple Pay and Google Pay need the Pool Junction customer app ($25/mo for the whole company). An optional $1.50 convenience fee can be added to each card payment and is paid by your customer. Its card processing rate isn't published. Price: $50/mo base plus $15/mo per tech. On 2026-11-24 the homepage banner also showed code BIG80NOW for 80% off for 3 months (Paythepoolman). {{aff:paythepoolman|Visit Paythepoolman}}

6. GorillaDesk: per-route pricing, subscriptions on Pro

GorillaDesk isn't pool-only (it also covers pest and lawn), but it prices per route with unlimited users. Basic ($49/mo for 1 route) includes invoices, advanced invoice frequencies, Stripe and Square payments and automated late-payment messages. Pro ($99/mo for 1 route) adds Stripe and Square subscription billing, the customer portal and QuickBooks Online sync. That sync is a one-way push to QuickBooks Online, and QuickBooks Desktop isn't supported. Processing is at Stripe's or Square's own rates (GorillaDesk pricing). Compare pool-specific features in Skimmer vs GorillaDesk. {{aff:gorilladesk|Visit GorillaDesk}}

How to choose

  • Mixed rate types. If some customers pay per stop and others a flat monthly rate, with chemicals included for some and extra for others, Skimmer and Pool Brain publish the most about handling both. For the others, test it with your own rates during the trial.
  • Billing ahead. If you charge at the start of the month, Skimmer (per-month rate type) and Pool Brain (advance billing) say they support it.
  • Card fees. No tool here publishes its card rate. Skimmer offers surcharging and Paythepoolman an optional $1.50 customer-paid convenience fee. Check your state's rules on surcharges before turning them on.
  • QuickBooks. Two-way sync: Pool Brain, POM (+$25/mo) and UpBuoy. Skimmer syncs in real time. GorillaDesk pushes one way and needs Pro. QuickBooks Desktop: only POM mentions it. More detail is in field service software with QuickBooks.
  • Cost. See pool service software cost and the pricing tracker. Before you commit, run one real billing cycle in the trial and use the software buying checklist.
faq: What is pool service invoicing software?

Software that turns the stops your techs log into customer invoices, usually as a monthly billing run, then collects payment online by card or bank, often on AutoPay. Skimmer, Pool Brain, Pool Office Manager, UpBuoy, Paythepoolman and GorillaDesk all list invoicing and online payments on their own pages (checked 2026-11-24).
Can pool software bill some customers per visit and others a flat monthly rate?

Skimmer's help center lists per-stop and per-month rate types, each with chemicals included or billed on top. Pool Brain's features page says billing can be per visit or flat rate, in advance or in arrears. The other tools here don't describe their rate types publicly (checked 2026-11-24).
Which pool service software has AutoPay?

Skimmer (customers enroll from an invoice or the portal), Pool Brain (automatic monthly charge with a daily retry on declined cards), UpBuoy and Paythepoolman list AutoPay. GorillaDesk offers automated subscription billing through Stripe or Square on its Pro plan. Pool Office Manager's pricing page doesn't mention AutoPay.
Can I pass credit card fees on to pool customers?

Skimmer lists credit card surcharging, and Paythepoolman offers an optional $1.50 convenience fee per card payment paid by the customer. The other tools don't publish a pass-through option. Surcharge rules vary by state and card network, so check them before turning it on.
What is the cheapest pool billing software?

At list prices for 1 tech: Paythepoolman $65/mo ($50 base + $15 per tech), GorillaDesk Basic $49/mo for 1 route (Pro, with subscription billing and QuickBooks, $99/mo), Pool Brain $115/mo and Pool Office Manager $125/mo. UpBuoy's Essential plan is free for up to 3 locations, but its advanced billing is on Professional ($3 per location, $99 minimum). Checked 2026-11-24.
